days.label: Monday
days.text: Monday leans musical. The big one is Gregory Alan Isakov with the Vermont Symphony Orchestra on the Green at Shelburne Museum at 7, the Colorado songwriter's hushed folk backed by a full symphony, and if you miss tonight he plays a second night Tuesday at 7. The Lake Champlain Chamber Music Festival keeps its run going all four days of this window with master classes, talks and performances around the county, full schedule at lccmf.org. Readers with a darker shelf can hit the new Queer/LGBTQ+ Horror Book Club at the Hunny Hive on Church Street at 5:30, this month's theme is mushrooms, and anyone with energy to burn can play dodgeball ($5) at the Miller Center in the New North End at 7. Performers, Lyric Theatre's auditions for Elf the Musical run tonight through Wednesday at 5:45 in South Burlington, first timers explicitly welcome, and the show lands at the Flynn in November. And in the department of small civic joys, Winooski neighbors are throwing an opening day joy ride on the new #9 bus to Shaw's , meeting at 10 East Allen at 7 to ride out, shop and catch the sunset from Water Tower Hill.

days.label: Tuesday
days.text: Tuesday has range. Early birds can hit the Small Business and Entrepreneurs Networking session at the South Burlington library at 8:30 with an expert panel and free coffee. After work, EZ Breezy Bike Rides roll a casual loop from Local Motion at 6, the Vermont Figure Drawing Collective ($20) hosts its weekly session at Karma Bird House at 6, and the Forever 38 crew's Ladies Book Club [MEETUP] talks Mad Mabel over dinner at Spot on the Dock at 6:15. Local Dork spins vinyl at Foam from 6 to 9, free as always, and board game people get a library game night at Essex Free at 6 with refreshments. Late crowd, DEAD.M.W. hits Einstein's Tap House at 9, members of Dopapod and Dobbs' Dead weaving Medeski Martin & Wood and Grateful Dead tunes for one of just two nights.

days.label: Wednesday
days.text: Wednesday is the fullest day on the calendar and the forecast agrees with it. Our own Pick-up Basketball [MEETUP] runs at Pomeroy Park at 5:30, outdoors and free, come get a run in. The Waterfront Silent Disco is the fun one, a sunset dance walk with wireless headsets popping up dance floors from the docks to the overlooks, meet at ECHO at 6:30. Cyclists can join the bike ride to Upper Pass Beer Co [MEETUP] leaving Simple Roots at 5:30, and daytime folks have two good ones, Plant Based Natural Dyeing at the Intervale at 11 where you take home a hand dyed silk handkerchief, and a Tree ID and Natural History Tour of Oakledge Park at noon, held by City Market. Singles, Seven Days throws its Singles Party at Four Quarters ($10) in Winooski at 6 with speed dating and mocktails, 21 plus and queer friendly. The evening keeps going with The All-Inclusive Dyke-Tacular at Doma Bar from 5, country night at Higher Ground's Showcase Lounge with Luke Borchelt and Troy Millette & the Fire Below at 8, league night at the Pinball Co-op in South Burlington as Season 11 gets going, and trumpeter Ray Vega's free weekly Jazz Night at Hotel Vermont at 8:30.

days.label: Thursday
days.text: Thursday stacks up nicely too. For our 21-39 crowd , we have our BTown Brief Trivia Night at J Skis [MEETUP] collab with South Burlington’s Young Social Pulse at 6, free to play, come say hi. Free pizza included! Would love to have more of these age-leaning events, so be sure to come out! Shelburne Summer Nights opens the museum free from 5 to 7:30 with food vendors, games and live music on the lawn. Dog people should not sleep on Bark & Brew at the Humane Society ($20) from 5:30, Foam, Weird Window and Black Flannel pouring while dogs romp in the play yard, proceeds to the shelter. The neighborhood option is Potlucks in the Park at Schmanska from 5:30, the season's last one, and South Burlington marks a year of City Center momentum at the SB3C annual event at Homewood Suites at 5:30 with free apps, drinks and the inside scoop on Leunig's coming to Market Street. There is also a weekly free wine tasting at La Reprise from 4 to 7, lawn games at the Essex Free Library garden at 6:30, and the Solarpunk Book Club & Game Night at the Peace & Justice Center early that evening. Night owls can pick between Lebanese NYC comedian Nataly Aukar ($25) at Vermont Comedy Club at 7, Spike Lee's Bamboozled at the VTIFF Screening Room at 7, and Thunderbolt Research playing free at Foam from 7 to 9.
